title: December 7, 2026 Claude Exam Update: What Changes
description: Three Claude exams get updated content on December 7, 2026, with new guides on November 17. Which exams change, what to study, and where the CCAR-F stands.

faq.q: Which Claude exams change on December 7, 2026?
faq.a: The Associate, Foundations (CCAO-F), Developer, Foundations (CCDV-F) and Architect, Professional (CCAR-P) exams include updated content starting December 7, 2026, according to the Claude Certification Program page on Pearson VUE.

faq.q: Is the CCAR-F exam part of the December 2026 update?
faq.a: No. Anthropic's certification page lists the same exam guide for the Architect, Foundations exam (CCAR-F, also written CCA-F) before and after December 7, 2026, so its current guide remains the reference.

faq.q: When will the updated Claude exam guides be published?
faq.a: The updated exam guides were published on November 17, 2026. Candidates who test on December 7 or later should prepare from the updated guide.

faq.q: Which guide should I use if my exam is before December 7?
faq.a: The current exam guide. The updated content applies from December 7, 2026, so an exam taken before that date follows the current guide.

body:
Anthropic's certification program has made its first content update. According to the Claude Certification Program page on Pearson VUE, which delivers the exams, three Claude exams include updated content starting on December 7, 2026, and the updated exam guides were published on November 17, 2026. If you are preparing for one of those exams, the date of your appointment decides which version you take. This post was updated on November 18, 2026 with what the new guides change.

Which exams change on December 7

The update covers three exams:

  • Claude Certified Associate, Foundations (CCAO-F)
  • Claude Certified Developer, Foundations (CCDV-F)
  • Claude Certified Architect, Professional (CCAR-P)

The Claude Certified Architect, Foundations (CCAR-F, also written CCA-F) exam is not part of the update: Anthropic's certification page lists the same exam guide for it before and after December 7. The page also lists a Professional-level Developer exam, with a single guide for both periods.

Taking the CCDV-F before December 7?

Practice on the current exam guide: 500 CCDV-F questions, each explaining the correct answer and why every other option is wrong, plus a full 53-question timed mock exam that draws a new set on every attempt. We will update the bank for the new guide for exams from December 7, at no extra cost to anyone enrolled.

Try 10 free CCDV-F questions See the CCDV-F practice bank

Preparing for the CCAR-F instead? Anthropic's December 7 update does not include that exam. See our 500 CCAR-F practice questions.

What is known, and what is not yet

The new guides are out, so the open questions now have answers. For the Developer exam, version 1.1 of the guide (CCDV-F) changes the format and the weights:

  • Items: 70, of which 60 are scored and 10 are unscored, up from 53. Unscored items are not identified.
  • Time and passing score: unchanged at 120 minutes and a scaled 720.
  • Item format: scenario-based multiple-choice items, each stating how many responses to select.
  • Weights: Applications and Integration falls from 33.1% to 20%, and Model Selection and Optimization from 16.8% to 12%. Eval, Testing, and Debugging rises from 2.6% to 10%, Claude Code from 3.1% to 8%, Prompt and Context Engineering from 11.0% to 15%, and Agents and Workflows from 14.7% to 17%. Tools and MCP (10%) and Security and Safety (8%) barely move.
  • Skills: the guide now lists 24 skills and no longer gives each one a weight. New topics include Claude Managed Agents, the Files API, grounding answers in supplied documents with citations, and calibrating LLM-as-judge evaluations.

For the Associate exam, version 1.1 of the guide (CCAO-F) describes 70 items, 60 of them scored, in 120 minutes across six domains, with a $99 fee. For the Architect, Professional exam, see its page on Anthropic's certification site.

If your exam is before December 7

You are taking the current exam, so the current exam guide is your syllabus. The new guide is out. Read it for interest, but do not let it pull your study time away from the scope you will actually be tested on.

For the Developer exam, Section 6 of the current guide (CCDV-F) weights eight domains, and Applications and Integration alone is 33.1% of the exam. Our four-week CCDV-F study plan turns those weights into a schedule, and the CCDV-F exam guide page summarizes the current format: 53 items in 120 minutes, including multiple-response items.

If your appointment falls close to the change, check the date carefully and settle it well in advance. Since November 12, 2026 you schedule, pay and make changes at Pearson, up to 1 hour before an online (OnVUE) exam or 48 hours before a test center exam. Our step-by-step registration guide covers the process.

If your exam is on or after December 7

Prepare from the updated guide, published on November 17, which leaves about three weeks before the first exams on the new content. A sensible way to use that window:

  • Compare the two blueprints first. Put the current and updated domain lists side by side and mark what is new, what moved and what changed weight.
  • Keep what still applies. Work you have already done on topics that remain in the blueprint still counts.
  • Spend the new time where the weight moved. A domain whose weight went up deserves more of your remaining hours than one that stayed the same.

For the CCDV-F, the weight has moved toward Eval, Testing, and Debugging, Claude Code, and Prompt and Context Engineering, and away from Applications and Integration.

If you are still choosing between exams, our comparisons of the Developer and Architect exams and of the Associate and Architect exams describe each exam under its current guide; the Developer comparison now notes the December 7 changes, and we will update the Associate comparison for its new guide.

If you are preparing for the CCAR-F

The Architect, Foundations exam is not part of this update. Its current guide describes 60 items in 120 minutes across five domains, led by Agentic Architecture and Orchestration at 27% (Sections 3 and 4 of the guide, CCAR-F). Your preparation plan does not need to change. A good starting point is the free CCAR-F diagnostic, which scores you by domain.

If you already hold a credential

A credential you have already earned stays valid for its 12 months. Both Foundations guides add one condition worth knowing: if exam content changes significantly, Anthropic may require holders to retake the full exam to recertify rather than complete the free renewal assessment (Section 14 of the CCDV-F guide, Section 15 of the CCAR-F guide). The December notice does not say whether that applies to this update, so watch for notices from the program as your renewal date approaches. Our guide to how renewal works covers the normal process.

What we are doing with our practice banks

  • CCDV-F: our CCDV-F practice bank is written to the current exam guide, the one that applies to exams taken through December 6. The updated guide was published on November 17, and we have checked the bank against it. For exams from December 7 we are adding questions where the weight moved, and the full mock exam moves to 70 items. Everyone enrolled keeps lifetime access and receives the update at no extra cost.
  • CCAR-F: the exam is not part of this update, so our 500 CCAR-F practice questions continue to follow its current guide.

You can try the Developer bank's style now with the free 10-question CCDV-F sprint, which needs no account.
